chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the compurgation (sworn oaths), how it was? So he said: 'It is truth, and it is written with us. And had it not been for that, the people would have killed each other, then nothing would remain. But rather, the compurgation is a salvation for the people.'

key_terms.الْقَسَامَةِ: Compurgation; a group of people swearing oaths to establish guilt or innocence, particularly in blood money cases.
key_terms.حَقٌّ: Truth; established reality or valid ruling.
key_terms.مَكْتُوبَةٌ: Written; recorded or documented in their sources.
key_terms.نَجَاةٌ: Salvation; deliverance or rescue from chaos/conflict.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of compurgation (qasamah) in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes al-qasamah as a divinely sanctioned mechanism for resolving homicide cases where the perpetrator is unknown, emphasizing its role in preventing chaotic blood feuds. The Imam highlights that this practice is not merely a legal formality but a crucial means of communal preservation ('salvation'), ensuring that justice is served without descending into endless vendettas. This underscores the Shia jurisprudential view of qasamah as a practical tool for social stability rooted in prophetic tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(The narrator) says, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the compurgation (sworn endorsements), how it was to be?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is truth, and it is written with us<sup>asws</sup>. And had it not been for that, the people would have killed each other, then nothing would happen. But rather, the compurgation (sworn endorsements) is a salvation for the people’.
